commits.message: Drop _endCells and Stops.end: a wrapped row's end stays a probe, so no layout shifts and a press past a row still lands on the end; keep a caret segment's control at the end slot; delete the uncalled shownOrder; scope the docs to the orders the frame orders; narrow the step oracle's skip to an unpressable line end (rich-control-codes-xh4n.tmh)

The end slot is a fact of its own: Style.textEnd marks the blank past the text on every path — probe, fallback, drawn caret, terminal caret, Dropdown — and ordering folds it into clusterLevels' 'level before it' rule; a press past a row lands on Stops.end (rich-control-codes-xh4n.tmh)

The caret past a mixed-direction text stands beside the last character typed: CaretMark.after marks the blank a widget adds past the text, and ordering gives it the level before it (rich-control-codes-xh4n.tmh)

Under logical, TextInput reads a press in the frame's order, the column the terminal reports (rich-control-codes-xh4n.wk5) (#567)

* Under logical, the router maps a pointer's column through the whole composed line to the frame's (writtenColumn), so a press inside a Panel lands where the terminal shows it; TextInput reads presses off the frame's order and steps off the shown one (rich-control-codes-xh4n.wk5)

* App.frameColumn owns the screen-to-frame column map, cached per painted line; the router asks it once per event; controls stay out of what UAX #9 orders; logical press tests drive the router (review of #567)

* Under logical a press reads the column the terminal reports, which is the frame's (VTE's vis2log): drop the router's screen-to-frame mapping, keep TextInput's press on its frame-order stops, and model the terminal's report in the tests (review of #567)

* A press past a row's cells lands on the stop shown beside it; the right-to-left page no longer lists pointer hits as a logical limit; press tests drive one router per input over one render, logical included in the direct press test (review of #567)
